submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 at 38.1 GeV is the best-performing choice in the simulation scan: among the three candidate algorithms it gives the highest observed average signal efficiency at the 8 kHz rate boundary, with 93.1063% average efficiency in the fine scan. The threshold is within the allowed 20–60 GeV range. However, the Level-1 FPGA latency was not available/verified for any candidate, so the hard <=4.0 us latency requirement remains unknown and must be confirmed before deployment.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: Allocated trigger rate is 8 kHz. Simulation results identify Algorithm-L1 as best: coarse best was Algorithm-L1 near 30–40 GeV, and the fine scan found the best average efficiency at 38.1 GeV with 93.1063%, higher than Algorithm-L3 and Algorithm-L2 summary/coarse efficiencies.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md contains 3 candidates; the recommendation selects Algorithm-L1, one of the listed candidates.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm's latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: Latency limit is 4.0 us, but recorded latencies for Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3 are all unknown; no candidate has latency eligibility confirmed (latency_confirmed_eligible_count = 0).
Recommended threshold is 38.1 GeV, which lies within the allowed 20–60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L1 with threshold 38.1 GeV.
